adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is uninstantiable: build_occurrence_and_event_data is now an abstractmethod on StatefulDetectorHandler but the redefined MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclass has no implementation, causing TypeError at runtime for metric-alert detectors

PriorityLevel(new_status) performs raw value-coercion between unrelated enums DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel; if values don't align it raises ValueError or silently maps to the wrong priority with no test or conversion helper enforcing the coupling

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel`, but the diff now calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`. This is a direct Enum construction that relies on the two enums’ underlying values being compatible; if they ever diverge it will raise `ValueError` or mis-map priorities. The diff does not show the enum definitions, so an actual mismatch can’t be verified, but the coupling risk introduced by this conversion is real and currently unguarded by an explicit mapping/helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests test_results_on_change and test_dedupe pass value 100/8 to evaluate but assert expected occurrence with value 6, encoding wrong expected inputs that will mislead future edits or hide propagation bugs

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py`, `test_results_on_change` calls `handler.evaluate(...{"val1": 100}...)` but constructs the expected occurrence via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)`, and `test_dedupe` similarly evaluates with `{"val1": 8}` but builds expected data with value `6`. While this mismatch does not currently affect the assertions because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument, it makes the tests misleading and could mask/allow future bugs if occurrence construction later starts using `value`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler does not implement newly added abstract methods (build_occurrence_and_event_data, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values), causing TypeError when instantiating handler for metric-alert detectors instead of previous no-op behavior

PriorityLevel(new_status) raw-value conversion between DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel can raise ValueError if enum values diverge, silently losing detector state updates for untested priority levels

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a direct enum conversion `PriorityLevel(new_status)` in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` when building an occurrence (`build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`). If `DetectorPriorityLevel` and `PriorityLevel` are not value-compatible, this can raise `ValueError` at runtime. The diff does not show the enum definitions, so we cannot verify that values currently diverge, nor that the failure would be “silent” (an exception would likely abort processing). However, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: process_detectors tests only assert the PayloadType.OCCURRENCE fire path; resolve path (StatusChangeMessage to Kafka) has no test verification

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, results are iterated and `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` is called whenever `result.result is not None`, which includes both the occurrence path and the resolve path where `result.result` is a `StatusChangeMessage` (see `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`: when `new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK`, it creates a `StatusChangeMessage`). The updated `TestProcessDetectors` only patches/asserts `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` for the occurrence path (`status_change=None`, `occurrence=...`) in `test_state_results` and `test_state_results_multi_group`, but there is no corresponding `process_detectors`-level test that drives `new_status == OK` and verifies Kafka production is called with a `StatusChangeMessage` (resolve path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-group-key guard and its test were deleted; no replacement safety net for DetectorHandler implementations returning colliding keys, and results dict signature change (tuple's second element now a dict) has no test covering downstream consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit duplicate `group_key` guard/logging in `process_detectors` (the `detector_group_keys` set and `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found")` block) and deletes the corresponding test (`test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`). The new `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, which inherently can’t represent duplicates; however, it can also silently drop/overwrite colliding keys (e.g., in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, `results[result.group_key] = result`) with no logging/safety net. The claim about “no test covering downstream consumers” of the changed return type isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (we can only see tests updated for `process_detectors` itself), but the removal of the duplicate-collision guard/test is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, so instantiating it raises TypeError (regression from working no-op to crash)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with an `evaluate()` implementation to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. In the same diff, `StatefulDetectorHandler` defines a new abstract method `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` (and already relies on other abstract hooks), so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` becomes abstract. If a `Detector` is configured to use this group type, `Detector.detector_handler` will attempt to instantiate it (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`), which would raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` — a regression from the prior instantiable no-op handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate detector state group-key detection/logging was deleted; the dict refactor now silently overwrites collisions with no log or metric

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit duplicate `group_key` detection/logging in `process_detectors`, but after the refactor `evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (and `StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values` is also a dict). Within the shown implementation, duplicate group keys cannot occur because dict keys are unique, and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` iterates `group_values.items()` (already de-duplicated) and produces one result per key. The finding’s claim about “silently overwriting collisions” is not supported by any collision-producing path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The only test for duplicate group-key behavior (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted with no replacement defining the new contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the handler/evaluation contract from returning a list of results to returning a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` (`DetectorHandler.evaluate` and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). With this new contract, “duplicate group keys” are not representable in the returned value, and the previous duplicate-detection/logging block in `process_detectors` is removed accordingly. The deleted `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` is testing behavior that no longer exists under the new API, so its removal is consistent with the refactor rather than an unaddressed missing test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests build expected occurrences with value=6 while actual evaluated values are 100, 200, and 8, so the mock ignoring the value argument makes the tests tautological and unable to detect wrong values passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple tests constructing the expected occurrence/event data with a hardcoded `value=6` even when the evaluated packet values differ (e.g. `test_results_on_change` uses `group_vals: {"val1": 100}` but calls `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)`; `test_dedupe` uses `8` but calls with `6`; `test_state_results_multi_group` calls `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...)` while `group_vals` has `"group_2": 10`). In addition, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., value, ...)` never uses the `value` parameter, so these tests cannot detect incorrect values being passed through `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. This is a concrete test-quality gap introduced/exposed by the diff, not an application correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public API signature change of process_detectors/DetectorHandler.evaluate (list to dict return type) plus test-class restructuring is scope drift bundled with the hook, breaking callers and preventing clean revert

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes a broad public-facing API change: `process_detectors(...)` now returns `list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]]` instead of a list of results, and `DetectorHandler.evaluate(...)`/`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate(...)` are changed from returning `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to a `dict[...]` (see `processors/detector.py` signature updates and the new dict-building logic in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). Tests are also substantially restructured (new `BaseDetectorHandlerTest`, moved helpers, removed duplicate-group test). This is a real scope/architecture concern bundled with the new occurrence hook, but the diff alone cannot prove it breaks external callers outside the touched code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is uninstantiable because it doesn't implement abstract methods get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, causing TypeError when Detector.detector_handler is called for this group type

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` and left as `pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract methods including `get_group_key_values(...)` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` (and it already requires other abstract methods like `get_dedupe_value(...)`). Since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of these, it remains abstract and cannot be instantiated; any call path that constructs it via `Detector.detector_handler` for that group type would raise `TypeError`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) raw integer cross-enum coercion between DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel fails with ValueError for DetectorPriorityLevel.MEDIUM since PriorityLevel has no MEDIUM member, after enqueue_state_update has already run causing state/occurrence divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a cross-enum conversion in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` via `PriorityLevel(new_status)` (where `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel`). If those enums ever diverge in values/members, this can raise at runtime. Also, `enqueue_state_update(...)` happens before the conversion/occurrence building, so an exception would occur after state-update staging, which is a fragile ordering. However, the specific claim that this *will* fail for `DetectorPriorityLevel.MEDIUM` because `PriorityLevel` lacks `MEDIUM` is not verifiable from the diff (enum definitions aren’t shown).

The suggested fix is to update the docstring to match the new return type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of duplicate-group-key guard in process_detectors replaced with last-write-wins dict overwrite in evaluate, so duplicate group keys will silently drop occurrences instead of logging

adjudication.rationale: The duplicate-group-key guard in `process_detectors` was removed because the handler API changed: `DetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (see signature change and callers iterating `detector_results.values()`). With a dict, duplicate keys from the evaluation output are structurally impossible at the call boundary—there is no longer a list that can contain duplicates to detect/log in `process_detectors`. In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, results are built from `group_values.items()` where `group_values` itself is a dict (`get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`), so duplicates cannot be produced there either. The finding’s claim that “duplicate group keys will silently drop occurrences instead of logging” misreads the new contract and the source type of group keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, breaking its previous safe no-op `return []` contract and causing TypeError on instantiation for metric-alert detector evaluation
Removed duplicate-group-key defensive guard in detector.py causes silent data loss of duplicate occurrences with no log, metric, or test, relying only on implicit invariant of unique keys

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (not a list) and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now builds that dict from `group_values.items()` where `group_values` itself is a dict (`get_group_key_values`), so duplicate group keys are not representable at this API boundary. The old duplicate-key guard in `process_detectors` was only relevant when iterating a list of results; with a dict, duplicates can’t occur without violating the contract, and the removed test (`test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`) relied on passing a list with duplicates which is no longer part of the new input shape (`group_vals` is a dict).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `Detector.group_type` @property (in `models/detector.py`) that resolves `grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type)` and returns `None` on miss, while `detector_handler` still contains the miss-handling/logging behavior (`logger.error(...)` when no grouptype). This introduces an additional, now-used entry point for grouptype resolution (tests call `detector.group_type` via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`), with different semantics (no logging), which is a maintainability/API-surface concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Expected occurrences in tests are generated by the same helper the mock handler delegates to, making equality assertions mirror-tests of the helper rather than independent expectations — a bug inside the helper appears on both sides of == and passes

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py`, `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` delegates to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)`. Multiple tests then construct the *expected* `occurrence, event_data` by calling the same `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` helper (e.g. `test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`, `TestEvaluate.test`, etc.) and assert equality against handler output. This makes those assertions dependent on the same helper logic on both sides, so a defect inside the helper could be mirrored and still pass. This is a test quality/independence issue rather than a production correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py is left abstract (StatefulDetectorHandler does not implement build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating it raises TypeError — a P1 crash with zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` but now only contains `pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` defines multiple `@abc.abstractmethod`s (e.g. `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of them, it remains abstract and attempting to instantiate it (as detector handlers are typically constructed for a detector’s group type) would raise `TypeError`. The diff also doesn’t add any test covering this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The RESOLVED/StatusChangeMessage path through process_detectors is never asserted at the producer level — no test mocks produce_occurrence_to_kafka for the status-change (DetectorPriorityLevel.OK) case

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, the loop now iterates `for result in detector_results.values()` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` whenever `result.result is not None` (which includes the `DetectorPriorityLevel.OK` path where `evaluate_group_key_value` sets `result` to a `StatusChangeMessage`). The updated tests mock and assert `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` only for the occurrence-producing (non-OK) cases (`test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`), while the OK/RESOLVED `StatusChangeMessage` path is only asserted at the return-value level (e.g. `test_above_below_threshold`) and does not mock/assert producer behavior. This is a concrete missing test for newly added/changed behavior, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler whose new build_occurrence_and_event_data is an @abc.abstractmethod, so instantiating the metric-alert handler raises TypeError until implemented

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` and left as `pass`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate group keys in detector.py results are now silently dropped when converted to a dict, with the duplicate-key error logging guard deleted, so occurrences for overwritten results are never built with no log or metric

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` and updates `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to build that dict from `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is itself a dict (`get_group_key_values`), so duplicate group keys are not representable at this stage. The removed duplicate-key logging guard in `process_detectors` applied to the old list-based API; with the new dict-based contract, there’s no verifiable scenario in this diff where duplicates arise and are “silently dropped” during conversion, nor where occurrences are skipped due to overwriting.
